name: Archil

modes.label: Sandbox, 1-32 vCPU / 0.25-64 GiB, $0.055 per vCPU-hour + $0.020 per GiB-hour (Developer or Team)
modes.commit_note: Developer has a $10/month minimum and Team a $500/month minimum. Metered usage counts toward the minimum.
modes.note: Pricing page: "CPU is metered at $0.055 per vCPU-hour and memory at $0.020 per GiB-hour." Same rate on Developer and Team. A 1 vCPU / 2 GiB sandbox costs $0.095/h; 2 vCPU / 4 GiB costs $0.19/h. A stopped or paused sandbox has no compute charge. Persistent sandboxes are generally available (Sept 2026). Free plan (1 vCPU-hour + 2 GiB-hours a month, hard caps) is not priced here. Checked 2026-11-08.

evidence.quote: Network policies are available on the Developer, Team, and Enterprise plans
A sandbox created without a policy on these plans has unrestricted egress.
On the Free plan, every sandbox uses a managed policy: egress is denied by default, except to these destinations:

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Includes 1 vCPU-hour and 2 GiB-hours a month (30 minutes of a 2 vCPU / 4 GiB sandbox), 1,000 serverless tool calls, 10 GB per disk on up to 5 disks. Hard caps, no overage. 5 concurrent sandboxes, 30-minute sessions. Egress reaches a managed allowlist (package registries, Git hosts, container registries, OS mirrors, model APIs).

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: $10/month minimum; metered usage counts toward it ("is not a fee added to usage"). 20 concurrent sandboxes. Unrestricted egress by default; network policies, firewall and credential brokering included.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $500/month minimum; metered usage counts toward it. 250 concurrent sandboxes (+500 for $500/month). SOC 2. Same per-resource rates as Developer.

plans.name: Enterprise (BYOC / on-prem)
plans.note: Custom minimum commitment, unlimited concurrency, BYOC (AWS, GCP, Azure, bare metal) or on-prem, PrivateLink / VPC peering, HIPAA with DPA and BAA, SSO & SCIM, SLA. Unpublished.

extras.price: $0.20/GiB-month on Developer and Team; Free: 10 GB per disk, up to 5 disks
$0.025/GB-month on paid plans for data on Archil-managed disks (disks synced to your own bucket do not pay it)
$0.07/GB on Developer and Team; free within Archil
$0.05 per 1,000 calls on Developer and Team, execution included; Free: 1,000 calls a month

perf_source: ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 2.48 s median at 100 at once, 100% succeeded (2026-11-06); DAX clone + install + typecheck 45.6 s (2026-11-06, one run; sandbox saw 8 CPUs / 16 GiB x86); one-at-a-time start 128 ms (sequential TTI, latest published run 2026-08-07 or older). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results
caveats: Sandboxes are metered per resource: $0.055 per vCPU-hour and $0.020 per GiB-hour for every size from 1 to 32 vCPU and 0.25 to 64 GiB (archil.com/pricing, 2026-11-08).
Developer ($10/month) and Team ($500/month) are minimums: metered usage counts toward them. The Free plan (1 vCPU-hour + 2 GiB-hours a month, 30-minute sessions, hard caps) is not used for pricing.
Billing granularity for sandbox time is not published.

A session pauses after at most 24 hours (30 minutes on Free), and after 30 idle minutes by default; the user can turn off the idle timeout. A pause keeps the root filesystem, mounted disks, memory and running processes, and resume continues the work.

Free plan egress reaches only a managed allowlist (package registries, Git hosts, container registries, OS mirrors, model APIs). Developer and above have unrestricted egress by default, at $0.07/GB out of Archil.
Docker and Docker Compose are supported (start the daemon first). /dev/kvm is not available, so no nested virtualization.
Disk priced at Archil active storage $0.20/GiB-month. Storage price of paused memory snapshots is not published (snapshot_gib_month null).
Prices are for AWS us-east-1; other regions vary with no published multiplier. Public sandbox regions are AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1); a GCP region exists for disks only.
Forks of running or paused sandboxes keep memory and disk; the docs give about 15 ms for a checkpoint and 35 ms for a branch, regardless of disk size.

Custom images: public and private Linux amd64 OCI images (default ubuntu:26.04). Private images are built first with registry credentials (not stored). Source: https://docs.archil.com/compute/sandboxes/images.
Sandbox ports can be exposed publicly (any TCP over TLS with SNI) or privately via port tokens (HTTP/1.1 over HTTPS).
Compliance: SOC 2 on Team; HIPAA with DPA and BAA on Enterprise (pricing page and security docs agree, 2026-11-08).

fleet.verification: No credit card needed to start; standard paid billing uses card via Stripe, Enterprise invoices.
fleet.notes: Concurrent sandbox limits per plan are published on the pricing page: 5 (Free), 20 (Developer), 250 (Team, +500 for $500/month), unlimited (Enterprise). Persistent sandboxes are generally available since September 2026.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A sandbox has a hard timeout and an optional idle timeout. Both pause the sandbox, preserving its disk, memory, and processes for `resume()`.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggered by the hard timeout (at most 24 h) or the idle timeout (30 minutes by default since Oct 2026, can be turned off); memory + running processes included. Traffic to an exposed port / port token auto-resumes a paused sandbox. Plain stop() is disk-only. Planned maintenance also pauses.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Checkpoints a running source sandbox and creates an isolated writable disk branch. Forks from running or paused sources resume from the source's CPU, memory, and disk state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: pause() snapshots CPU+memory+disk on demand; fork() of a running/paused/stopped sandbox creates new sandboxes from that state (memory included unless source stopped). No separate named-snapshot object for sandboxes; Archil disks additionally have branches/checkpoints.

harness_api.note: Full docs corpus (llms-full.txt) searched: only a generic processes/exec + PTY API; no Claude Code/Codex/etc. driver. AI guides use AI SDK with disk.exec as a bash tool (harness runs outside).

egress_allowlist.quote: The sandbox firewall operates on both the IP and transport layer, so you can filter both CIDR ranges and domains.
egress_allowlist.note: Default allow/deny + allow/deny lists (IPv4/CIDR, exact or *. wildcard domains); live-updatable via updateNetwork. "Network policies are available on the Developer, Team, and Enterprise plans". Free uses a managed allowlist policy.

egress_http_rules.quote: Allowed IPv4 addresses, CIDR ranges, exact domains, wildcard domains beginning with `*.`, or target objects with optional outbound HTTPS request transformations.
egress_http_rules.note: Rules match on host/IP only (rule schema is closed: target, transform.headers, forward_url). Header injection and forward_url (send matching requests to your own HTTPS endpoint, which could filter) exist, but no method/path/header matching.

ingress_rules.quote: For private access, leave the port unexposed and create a port token. Send the token in the `X-Archil-Token` header; requests without a valid token get `401`.
ingress_rules.note: Choose which ports to expose (public, any TCP over TLS+SNI, no auth) or keep private with expiring port tokens (HTTP/1.1 over HTTPS). Services private unless enable_service_ingress. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Full Linux microVM, processes run as root (uid 0); not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: This means that secret credentials can live outside the sandbox, so untrusted workloads cannot access them directly. For example, you can add API keys to outgoing HTTP requests so your sandbox never sees them:
secret_proxy.note: Per-domain header transforms on the TLS-terminating egress proxy (Archil CA installed in sandbox). HTTP(S) only (ports 80/443); no DB/SSH/git-over-SSH coverage. Developer plan and above.

volume_attach.quote: The Archil CLI comes prebaked into sandboxes, so you can attach an Archil disk to a sandbox by using the usual command to mount the disk:
volume_attach.note: Archil disks (S3-backed elastic POSIX FS) mounted from inside via `archil mount` with a mount token; each sandbox also has its own dedicated persistent disk.

volume_shared.quote: Archil supports sharing disks between multiple connected users simultaneously.
volume_shared.note: Read-write with delegations: exclusive mode (one machine), shared mode (read-only until `archil checkout <path>` write-lock), conditional mode (NFS-like, all unlocked files writable).

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization | Not supported: `/dev/kvm` is not available inside the sandbox.
nested_virt.note: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM; /dev/kvm is not exposed.

anti_bot.quote: Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
anti_bot.note: Outside the product scope: Archil is a disk + sandbox + serverless-execution platform with no browser or stealth features in the docs.

captcha_solving.quote: Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
captcha_solving.note: Outside the product scope: no browser or CAPTCHA features in the docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: our egress proxy must terminate TLS, so we install an "archil egress" proxy CA into every sandbox
egress_ip_type.note: Sandboxes run on AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) and egress passes through Archil's own TLS-terminating egress proxy fleet; this is standard cloud/datacenter IP space, not residential/mobile. No specific IP range or static-IP guarantee is published.

ssh.note: No SSH access to persistent sandboxes is documented anywhere in the docs or API reference; interaction is via the processes/exec API and exposed TCP/HTTPS ports (public ports or private port tokens), not SSH. The only SSH content in the docs is an unrelated guide for self-hosting Archil inside your own Firecracker microVM.

live_resize.note: vCPU/RAM (1-32 vCPU, 0.25-64 GiB) are set only at sandbox creation. The full sandbox API surface (create/start/stop/pause/resume/fork/set-timeout/update-network/expose-port) has no update-resources/resize endpoint.

own_agent_api.quote: Run untrusted AI-generated code against context with tools based on serverless execution or traditional persistent sandboxes.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Archil provides generic compute/exec + disk storage for others to build agents on top of; it does not ship its own browser/computer-use/research task agent or an API to drive one.

mcp_server.quote: Add to your agent, [Mastra](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@archildata/mastra), or [LangChain](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@archildata/langchain). For more control, use our TypeScript SDK or Python SDK directly.
mcp_server.note: Docs list integrations (Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain) and TypeScript/Python/CLI SDKs, but no MCP server package or docs page exists anywhere in the full docs corpus.

lang_python.quote: Archil's serverless execution makes it simple to run untrusted code like bash, Python, and Node.js
lang_python.note: Also has a first-party Python SDK (docs.archil.com/sdks/python), and persistent sandboxes can boot any OCI image including python:3.13.

lang_node.quote: Archil's serverless execution makes it simple to run untrusted code like bash, Python, and Node.js
lang_node.note: Also has a first-party TypeScript/Node SDK (`disk` npm package) and persistent sandboxes can boot node:24-bookworm images.

max_session_h.quote: A session pauses after at most 24 hours.
max_session_h.note: The hard timeout pauses, not kills; resume keeps memory and processes and starts a new session. Free sessions are capped at 30 minutes. An idle sandbox also pauses after 30 minutes by default ("30 minutes without a process connection by default, then the sandbox pauses."); the user can turn this off.

fork_running.quote: Checkpoints a running source sandbox and creates an isolated writable disk branch. Forks from running or paused sources resume from the source's CPU, memory, and disk state. ... A running source is resumed after its checkpoint; paused and stopped sources remain inactive.
fork_running.note: Fork a running, paused or stopped sandbox; running and paused sources keep CPU, memory and disk state. "A checkpoint takes about 15 ms and a branch about 35 ms, regardless of disk size." Sandboxes with mounted disks must be stopped first.

desktop.quote: Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
desktop.note: No desktop is provided and the docs have no desktop example. Sandboxes boot any amd64 OCI image (1-32 vCPU), so a user can put a desktop and a streaming server in a custom image and run it at their own effort.

browser.quote: Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
browser.note: No managed browser and no browser example in the docs. A user can install a browser in a custom OCI image.

computer_use.note: Only a generic process/exec + PTY API is offered; no screenshot+click computer-use API exists. Consistent with no desktop/browser being offered at all.

agent_harnesses.note: Full docs corpus searched for Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode: none found preinstalled or offered as a template. Only generic exec/process API + AI-SDK-as-bash-tool guides (harness runs outside the sandbox). Matches existing harness_api:false evidence.

public_ipv4.quote: Exposed ports are public: they accept any TCP protocol over TLS with SNI, without authentication. ... For private access, leave the port unexposed and create a port token.
public_ipv4.note: Sandbox ports are reached via a TLS/SNI hostname or private port token, never a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine. No mention of a per-sandbox public IPv4 anywhere in the docs.

gpu.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory.
gpu.note: Sandbox spec is CPU/RAM only; no GPU instance type mentioned anywhere in pricing or docs (only unrelated mentions of faiss-gpu, a client library, in a tutorial).

windows.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory. Sandboxes run as the root...
windows.note: Sandboxes are Linux microVMs (custom images default to ubuntu); no Windows machine type is offered. Windows only appears in the docs as a client-OS caveat for the CLI/download tables, not as a sandbox OS.

macos.quote: Persistent sandboxes are built on full-featured Linux microVMs that are colocated with your Archil disk data...
macos.note: Compute (sandboxes) is Linux-only. Archil does ship a macOS *client* app (Archil for macOS, FSKit menu-bar app) for mounting disks locally, but that is not a macOS compute/sandbox machine, so the feature (macOS machines offered) is correctly false.

arm64.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory.
arm64.note: Sandbox compute is explicitly x86-64 only. arm64 binaries exist only for the client CLI/Lambda layer, not for sandbox machines.

self_host.quote: [contact us](mailto:support@archil.com) to learn more about our BYOC options for organizations with 100 TiB of data
self_host.note: Enterprise BYOC (AWS, GCP, Azure, bare metal) or on-prem with Archil operating it; no self-managed open build.

open_source.quote: This page covers versioned, signed Linux releases only. It does not cover macOS, Windows, package-repository signing, Sigstore or Cosign attestations, or the unversioned `https://archil.com/install` script.
open_source.note: Only compiled client binaries/CLI and SDKs are distributed (no OSI-license source repo for the core sandbox/storage engine found in docs or a public GitHub org); the core Archil disk/sandbox engine is proprietary.

docker_inside.quote: Docker and Docker Compose | Supported. Start the Docker daemon inside the sandbox before using it.
docker_inside.note: Sandboxes support running containers inside the VM.

static_egress_ip.quote: our egress proxy must terminate TLS, so we install an "archil egress" proxy CA into every sandbox
static_egress_ip.note: All sandbox internet egress (Developer plan and above; Free uses a managed allowlist) is routed through Archil's own shared TLS-terminating egress proxy fleet, matched by domain/CIDR allow-deny rules. Docs never publish a fixed/dedicated outbound IP (or IP range) per sandbox or per account that a customer could allowlist on a third-party service; the egress feature set (firewall, allow/deny lists, header-injection secret proxy) is documented in detail with no mention of a static IP option, so it is treated as not offered rather than merely undocumented.

usage_api.quote: The Archil Control Plane API provides programmatic access to manage disks, mounts, and API keys. [Lists endpoints for Disks, Serverless Execution, Sandboxes, but no Usage or Metering endpoint]
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Billing page shows usage monitoring via console dashboard (Usage tab per disk, account-wide Billing page with real-time charts), but no REST API endpoint exists for programmatic usage retrieval per sandbox or by tag/project. Usage is only available dashboard for account.

custom_image.quote: Archil supports public and private Linux images built for `amd64`.
custom_image.note: Public images via baseImage (Docker Hub shorthand or full reference, default ubuntu:26.04). Private: "For a private image, build it with your registry credentials first." then create with imageId; "Archil does not store these credentials, so supply them each time you build."

image_oci.quote: Start sandboxes from public or private OCI images and reuse prepared images.

hipaa.quote: We sign **Business Associate Agreements (BAAs)** with [Enterprise plan](/administration/billing) customers.
hipaa.note: BAA on Enterprise. The pricing page now also lists HIPAA, DPA and BAA under Enterprise only, so the old Team conflict is gone.

persist_scope.quote: Keeps the root filesystem, mounted disks, memory, and running processes.
persist_scope.note: Pause keeps the whole disk plus memory; stop() shuts the VM down and keeps the disk.

locations_quote: Prices are for AWS us-east-1; 'other regions vary' with no multiplier published. Sandboxes run in AWS regions only (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
